No singer is credited; the authored palette follows this complete three-instrument credit sheet rather than assuming uncredited vocals or synthesizers. The June2020 digital release explicitly identifies original January2006 issue. Japanese prog is a national progressive/experimental-rock network: the creator map includes Ruins, KENSO, Ars Nova, Koenjihyakkei, Sadistic Mika Band and Acoustic Asturias. The selected Ruinzhatova collaboration is on the Ruins artist-run release page and explicitly described as Japanese progressive free-rock; it is not asserted to be a separate creator-map member. Existing progressive_rock describes the classic UK-rooted composition-centered tradition and later revival, whereas this national network encompasses a documented free-improvising branch. Existing zeuhl and zeuhl_french legitimately include Japanese followers; Japanese prog is not equivalent to that narrower Magma-derived Kobaian/ostinato lineage. Existing japanese_psychedelic_rock and japanoise overlap artists but describe respectively psychedelic repetition/fuzz and saturated noise practice, not the whole documented progressive network. This is an overlapping regional umbrella, not a claim all Japanese progressive music has one distinct sound. Broad experimental-rock parent is limited to the selected extended free-rock improvisation rather than asserting composed classical suites. Authored rendition uses an alder/maple humbucker guitar with overdriven single-note lead, compatible alder/maple dual-single-coil fingerstyle bass, and conventional rock kit.
